Laura / team — draft guidance below for Acme. Happy to sign off once they confirm which banks/rails they'll use for each leg.

EUR leg (preferred):

- Bank: Continental Eurobank
- IBAN: GB29CONT12345678901234
- BIC/SWIFT: CONTGB2L
- Reference: INV-2026-0157 | ACME EU PAY | partial EUR xx,xxx.

USD leg (APAC -> USD):
- Beneficiary: Redwood Inference, Inc. (US Collections)
- Bank: Northern Chase Bank
- Account: 4123456789
- Routing (ABA): 021000021
- Reference: INV-2026-0157 | ACME APAC PAY | partial USD xx,xxx.

Intermediary/correspondent fees:
- If Acme's SG bank sends EUR via a correspondent chain (multi-hop), their bank may apply an intermediary fee that can either be borne by the payer (OUR) or deducted from the transferred amount (SHA/BEN).
- Operationally we prefer to receive gross funds (OUR) so we don't have to reconcile shortfalls, but we understand some banks don't support OUR. If their bank only supports SHA or BEN (payer deducts), we need: 1) an itemized remittance showing the gross amount of the EUR leg, 2) the exact fee amount(s) deducted and 3) the final net amount received so we can reconcile to INV-2026-0157.

Reconciliation & invoice handling:
- We can accept two wires against a single invoice provided remittance data includes: invoice number, allocated amount (EUR vs USD), and payer entity name for each leg.
- Preferred: Acme issues a short remittance CSV (sample template attached) listing both transfers and allocation amounts. That will speed matching.
- If Acme prefers separate invoices for each legal entity, we can re-issue two invoices (EU and APAC) but that will affect VAT handling for the EU leg.

Next steps: If you confirm their bank details for each leg, I will provide an official wire instruction PDF for accounting and treasury.

—Rafael

Quick VAT note for routing:

- Since Acme says they have an EU VAT ID, the EU leg is B2B and should generally be treated under the reverse-charge mechanism — Redwood does not charge VAT if we have a valid VAT ID and evidence of intra-EU B2B supplies. We need: customer VAT ID, billing address for the EU entity, and the EU entity name exactly as on their VAT registration.
- If they instead pay via the APAC entity for the full invoice or without providing VAT ID, we need to charge VAT on the EU portion where applicable and reissue an invoice showing VAT separated.

So operational options:
1) Acme supplies VAT ID + sends EUR from EU entity -> no VAT charged on EU line, provide remittance mapping.
2) They send EUR from APAC entity or do not supply VAT ID -> we reissue EU invoice with VAT and collect accordingly.

I'll attach a short checklist we can send to Acme to avoid back-and-forth.

Marissa
Head of Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

3) However, our SG bank warned that when we convert SGD->EUR or SGD->USD there can be routing that results in a correspondent fee (they quoted possible ~15-25 USD equivalent). They asked if Redwood will accept net-of-fees or whether Acme should pay the fee on top.

- For the minimal intermediary fee (if it applies), we'll cover it (OUR) if necessary but would prefer to avoid re-issuing. If Redwood prefers OUR, confirm and we'll ask treasury to mark charges accordingly.

Attachments: wire_template.csv, INV-2026-0157.pdf

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
